question: What is the primary danger of running out of injection safety commodities at a health clinic?

options.A: Clinicians may resort to reusing single-use equipment.
options.B: Medications will automatically expire much faster.
options.C: The cost of electricity at the facility will increase.
options.D: Patients will completely stop visiting the facility for care.

explanation: When basic injection supplies run out, desperate staff may unfortunately reuse disposable syringes, spreading infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is accurate quantification of injection commodities important for a healthcare facility?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for medical waste disposal.
options.B: It reduces the total number of nursing staff needed on duty.
options.C: It guarantees that every patient will receive an antibiotic.
options.D: It prevents dangerous stockouts and costly item expiration.

explanation: Good estimation ensures enough supplies are available to prevent shortages while avoiding excess stock that expires on the shelf. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a conventional disposable syringe?

options.A: It can be washed and sterilized multiple times safely.
options.B: It locks or breaks automatically to prevent second use.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of liquid than any other type.
options.D: It is made entirely of soft, flexible rubber material.

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a built-in mechanism that renders them completely unusable after one single stroke. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a safety box in a clinical injection setting?

options.A: To measure precise doses of liquid drugs for patients
options.B: To store brand-new, sterile syringes away from dust and moisture
options.C: To transport mixed liquid medications safely to the bedside
options.D: To safely collect used needles and syringes before disposal

explanation: Safety boxes are puncture-resistant containers built specifically to hold used sharp items and protect staff from accidental needle sticks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why is a waste factor or buffer stock added when calculating injection commodities?

options.A: To provide extra income for the hospital pharmacy department
options.B: To ensure the facility has extra funds to pay staff salaries
options.C: To cover dropped items, training breakage, and accidental contamination
options.D: To account for patients who refuse to take their medications

explanation: A buffer percentage ensures unexpected item loss on the ward does not lead to a sudden shortage of clinical tools. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: A clinic notices a sudden influx of new patients moving into the local community. How should this affect their commodity calculations?

options.A: The safety box requirements should be completely ignored.
options.B: The clinic should switch exclusively to glass syringes.
options.C: The waste factor percentage must be reduced to zero.
options.D: The projected target population must be increased.

explanation: An increasing population means more people will need injections, requiring an upward adjustment in commodity estimation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: An immunization campaign targets 500 children, and each child requires 3 doses. Using a 10% waste factor, how many total syringes are needed?
explanation: First multiply 500 children by 3 doses to get 1,500 base items. Then multiply 1,500 by 1.10 (adding the 10% waste factor) to get 1,650. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: A local clinic plans to administer 4,000 curative injections over the next quarter without a waste factor. If each injection needs one syringe, how many syringes should be ordered?
explanation: Multiplying the total injection encounters by the dose per encounter without a waste factor gives the exact baseline total of 4,000. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h4)

question: What must a nurse always do when a calculated safety box requirement results in a fractional number like 12.3 boxes?

options.A: Always round up to the next whole number.
options.B: Ignore the calculation and request an arbitrary box amount.
options.C: Discard the fraction and order only the exact whole integer.
options.D: Always round down to the nearest lower whole number.

explanation: Rounding up ensures you never run out of disposal containers for your used needles and syringes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: A clinic expects to use 2,000 syringes during a vaccination drive. If each safety box holds 100 syringes, how many safety boxes are required?
explanation: Divide the total number of used syringes (2,000) by the capacity of a single box (100), which equals 20 boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when estimating injection commodity needs?

options.A: Performing regular physical inventory audits on the ward
options.B: Ignoring existing stock levels currently sitting in the storeroom
options.C: Collaborating closely with pharmacy and supply chain personnel
options.D: Reviewing past consumption reports from previous months

explanation: Always subtract what is already in stock from your calculated requirement so you do not accidentally over-order. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why is it a major mistake to order powdered vaccines without ordering reconstitution syringes?

options.A: The powder cannot be safely mixed into a liquid solution for injection.
options.B: The nursing staff will be unable to document the doses on paper.
options.C: Patients will experience immediate allergic reactions to the dry powder.
options.D: The safety boxes will instantly melt when exposed to powdered medicine.

explanation: Powdered vaccines or medications must be diluted with a liquid using special mixing syringes before they can be drawn up and administered. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)
